When AI developers train a massive model, they usually save it in high-precision formats—essentially 4K video files for math. Every single connection in that neural network is stored with extreme detail, using 16-bit or even 32-bit numbers. That sounds precise, but it also means the file is enormous, and your GPU has to crunch through a lot of data to run it. For a gamer buying their first card, that is usually a dealbreaker. You might have a decent RTX 4070 or 4080, but loading a 70-billion-parameter model in full precision could require 140 gigabytes of VRAM—more than your entire system has.

Quantization is the process of squeezing that high-definition file down without losing the plot. Instead of storing every weight with perfect precision, you round them to simpler values, often reducing them to 8-bit, 4-bit, or even lower. It is like telling your GPU, "You don’t need to know the exact shade of every pixel; just tell me if it’s dark or light." import asyncio
import time
from collections import OrderedDict
from typing import Any, Callable, Generic, Hashable, Optional, TypeVar

class AsyncLRUCache(Generic[T]):
    """A thread-safe (asyncio-safe) LRU cache with per-entry TTL.

    This cache uses an ``OrderedDict`` to maintain insertion/access order
    and an ``asyncio.Lock`` to ensure that concurrent coroutines do not
    corrupt the internal state. Each entry can have its own time-to-live
    (TTL) in seconds; expired entries are evicted lazily upon access.

    Attributes:
        max_size: Maximum number of entries the cache can hold.
        default_ttl: Default TTL (seconds) applied when ``ttl`` is not
            specified in :meth:`put`.
    """

    def __init__(self, max_size: int = 128, default_ttl: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Initialize the cache.

        Args:
            max_size: Maximum number of items to store. Must be > 0.
            default_ttl: Default time-to-live in seconds. A value of 0.0
                means entries never expire by default.
        """

            raise ValueError("max_size must be positive")
